What is the use of all the learning someone has acquired if they do not worship the good feet of the one who is pure knowledge?

Someone who meditates on the feet of a god who has no desire or aversion will never experience suffering.
Those who love the true praise of God are not affected by the good and bad deeds that come from ignorance.
Those who follow the true path of the one who has destroyed the five desires that arise from the five senses will live long.
Anxiety cannot be relieved for those who are not united with the feet of the incomparable one.
Only those who are united to the feet of the gracious Being who is a sea of virtue can swim the sea of vice. Others cannot cross the ocean of birth and death.
A head that does not bow to God, who has eight virtues, is as useless as a sense organ that cannot function.
Only those who are united with God's feet can swim across the great sea of birth, while those who are not united with them will drown in it.
The world continues to exist because of the unending rain, so rain is rightly called ambrosia.
Rain produces food for people to eat and is also a drink for them.
If the rain clouds fail to bring rain, hunger will torment and kill people in the vast world surrounded by the sea.
If the rain that brings wealth diminishes, the ploughman will not plough with his oxen.
Rain can destroy people by not falling, and it can save those who have lost everything by falling.
If no drop of rain falls from the clouds, it is rare to see even the head of a green blade of grass.
If the clouds do not give back the water they take from the ocean, even the vast ocean will lose its wealth. This is like how a society thrives only when its successful people contribute back to it.
If the sky doesn't rain, then people on earth will not perform any festivals or daily worship for the gods.
If the rain does not fall, the two virtues of giving to others and self-discipline will not exist in the world.
If there is no water, the world cannot exist, and without rain, there can be no order.
The greatness of those who have given up everything for their own code of conduct is the highest praise found in the best texts.
It is impossible to measure the greatness of those who have given up worldly desires, just as it is impossible to count all the people who have died in the world.
The greatness of those who understand the nature of both life and death and practice virtue in this world is supreme.
Someone who uses the hook of firmness to restrain the five senses is like a seed for the best place in the world to come.
Indra, the king of the heavens, is proof of the power of someone who has destroyed the five senses.
Great people do difficult things, while small people do easy things.
The world belongs to the one who understands the nature of the five senses: taste, sight, touch, hearing, and smell. This person can control the desires that arise from these senses.

The greatness of people who speak words of complete meaning will be displayed to the world by the magical words they have spoken. The enduring, powerful words they utter on earth will show their greatness.
The anger of those who have climbed the mountain of goodness, even if it lasts only for a moment, is impossible to endure.

A true householder is someone who firmly supports the three natural orders in the right way. These three orders are the teacher, the student, and the renunciate.

A person who lives a family life is considered a true companion if they help those who have renounced the world, the destitute, and those who have died. They provide support to the former through rituals, to the poor by giving them food, and to the dead by performing last rites.
The chief duty is to properly serve the five groups: ancestors, gods, guests, relatives, and oneself. This involves following the correct conduct for each of these five without fail.
Someone who avoids sinful ways of earning wealth and shares their food with others will never lose their prosperity or lineage.
If a household has love and virtue, these are its character and its benefit.
If someone lives a virtuous life in a family, what benefit can they gain by becoming a monk?
Among those who strive for happiness, the one who lives a domestic life according to its nature is the greatest.
A life of virtue that guides others and never strays is stronger than the endurance of ascetics.
A virtuous home life is praised as true virtue, and a monastic life is also good if it is not blamed by others.
Someone who lives a virtuous married life on earth will be honored among the gods in heaven.

A good wife possesses the virtues and skills suitable for the home, and she manages the household in a way that matches her husband's wealth. A woman who has these qualities and runs her family according to her husband's income is a true life partner.
A home is not a home without a virtuous wife, even if it has great wealth and splendor. A life without a wife who has good qualities is worthless, no matter how many other good things it has.
If a wife is virtuous, what does a man not have? If she is not virtuous, what does he have?
What is more valuable than a woman who has the firmness of chastity?
A wife who ignores God and worships her husband instead, and who will do whatever he commands, can make it rain just by saying the word.
A good wife protects her own character, takes care of her husband, and maintains their shared good reputation without ever getting tired or losing her resolve.
What is the use of guarding a woman in a prison? Her chastity is the greatest protection.

Women who respect their husbands and fulfill their duties will attain great glory in the world where the gods live. If women cherish their husbands as their leaders, they will gain great excellence in the world of the gods.
A man whose wife does not seek praise cannot walk with a proud, lion-like gait before those who revile him.
A virtuous wife is the true blessing of a home, and having good children is the beautiful ornament that enhances that blessing.
Among all the gains a person can get, there is no greater gain than having wise and virtuous children.
If you have children with good character who are free from blame, no evils or sorrows will touch them across all seven births.
People call their children their wealth, and that wealth comes from the children's actions.
Food that a child has touched with their small hands is sweeter to a parent than nectar.
The touch of children brings pleasure to the body, and hearing their words brings pleasure to the ear.
People who have never heard their own children's babbling are the ones who say the flute and lute are sweet.
A father's greatest benefit to his son is to make him learned so he can take the highest seat in an assembly of wise people.
A parent's joy at seeing their child's wisdom surpass their own is even sweeter to the rest of the world than it is to the parent.
A mother feels greater joy when she hears her son praised as wise than she did when she gave birth to him.
A son's true service to his father is to make people say, "What great penance did the father perform to beget such a son?
There is no lock that can keep true love hidden, because a single teardrop from a loving person will reveal it.
Those without love consider everything their own, while those with love consider even their own bones to belong to others.
The continuous connection between the body and the precious soul is the reward for the good deeds and love accumulated in a past life.
Love creates a deep desire to connect with others, and that desire brings about the boundless excellence of true friendship.
The special bliss that people who live happily in this world attain is the reward for living a life of love with their family.
Unwise people claim that love is only a support for virtue, but it also helps against evil. They do not realize that love is also a support for courage.
Virtue will burn the soul that lacks love, just as the sun burns the boneless worm.
A life without love is like a withered tree sprouting in a desert.
If someone lacks love in their heart, all their external body parts, wealth, and status are useless to them.
A body is alive only when it is guided by love; without love, it is just skin covering bone.
The purpose of earning and protecting wealth at home is to be able to host guests and help them.
Even if you are eating food that prevents death, it is not good to eat alone while keeping guests outside.
A person who consistently hosts guests every day will not suffer from poverty or have their life ruined.
The goddess of wealth will happily reside in the home of someone who welcomes worthy guests with a cheerful, smiling face.
Should a person sow their field if they first feed their guests and eat what is left? Their field will not yield a harvest.
Someone who takes care of a guest who has arrived and also looks forward to the next guest to come will be a welcome guest for the inhabitants of heaven in the afterlife.
The benefit of entertaining guests cannot be measured by any standard, as the value of the hospitality is determined solely by the worthiness of the guests themselves.

Those who do not practice hospitality will lament that they have worked hard to save wealth, only to lose it and have no support. They will regret that their wealth was not used for the ritual of hosting guests.
Someone who has wealth but does not honor guests is truly poor. This foolishness belongs only to stupid people.

A flower called anicham wilts the moment you smell it, and similarly, a guest wilts when they are looked at with a cold, turned-away face. The sources agree that a guest is even more delicate than this flower, which means a host must always welcome them with a smiling face.
Sweet words are spoken by people who know the truth, and they are full of love and free from deceit.
A smiling face and kind words are better than giving a gift with a happy heart.
True virtue is speaking sweet words from the heart with a pleasant look and a smiling face.
Those who speak sweet words that bring pleasure to everyone will not experience the sorrow of poverty.
Humility and speaking sweet words are the only true ornaments for a person; all other adornments are not.
If someone seeks out good and speaks sweet words that benefit others, their sins will diminish and their virtue will grow.
Words that give a beneficial advantage to others and never depart from good character bring happiness and goodness to the speaker, and yield righteousness for this world and merit for the next.
Sweet words that are free from meanness and do not cause pain to others will bring happiness in this world and in the next.
If someone knows that sweet words bring happiness, what is the use of using harsh words?
Speaking harsh words when sweet ones are available is like eating unripe fruit when ripe fruit is present.
If someone helps you even when you have never helped them before, the earth and the heavens combined cannot repay that favor.
A small favor done at the right time is more valuable than the entire world.
Helping someone without expecting a reward is a benefit that is greater than the sea.
If someone gives a small help as tiny as a millet seed, those who know its benefit will consider it as large as a palm tree.
The value of a returned favor is measured by the character of the person who received it, not by the size of the original favor.
You should never forget the friendship of people with a pure character, and you should not abandon the friends who supported you during times of trouble.
Good people will remember the friendship of those who wiped away their suffering through all seven of their births.
It is not good to forget a good deed done by someone, but it is good to forget a bad deed done by them on that very day.
Even if someone who previously helped you later commits a deadly harm like murder, remembering just one good deed they did for you will erase all that harm.
Someone who has destroyed great virtues may still find a way to escape, but there is no escape for someone who has destroyed a benefit.
Equity is a supreme virtue, which means giving each person their due without bias. This means treating enemies, strangers, and friends equally and justly without showing favoritism.
The wealth of a just person does not perish and will protect their descendants.
Even if unjust gains bring benefits, abandon them immediately.
A person's worthiness or unworthiness is judged by the character of their descendants, as well as by their wealth, fame, and the conduct of their children.
Loss and gain happen for a reason, and it is the wise person's ornament to remain even-minded in both situations.
If a person abandons justice and decides to do wrong, they should know that they are heading toward ruin.

When a person who lives justly and maintains a balanced life falls into poverty, the world will not consider it a true loss. Instead, people will respect them for their virtue rather than looking down on them as poor.
A wise person's beauty is their ability to remain perfectly impartial, like a balance scale that weighs things fairly without leaning to either side.
True justice is being completely unbiased in your mind and speaking without any crookedness.
A trader who treats others' property as his own will have a successful trade.
Self-control elevates a person to the realm of the gods, while a lack of self-control leads them into the deepest darkness.
Guard self-control as a treasure, because there is no greater gain for a living being than that.
Knowing that controlling oneself is true wisdom, if a person lives a disciplined life, their self-control will be recognized by good people and bring them great distinction.
A person who remains firm in their station and controls themselves will be greater than a mountain.
Humility is good for everyone, but for the wealthy, it is like having another special kind of wealth.

If someone controls their five senses during a single birth just as a tortoise pulls its five body parts into its shell, that discipline acts as a protective shield for them across seven future births.
Even if you fail to guard everything else, you should at least guard your tongue, because failing to do so will lead to the misery of making a mistake with your words.
If a person speaks even one evil word that causes harm to others, all the good they have done will be turned into evil.
A wound from fire can heal, but a wound from the tongue never does.
Virtue waits for the right time to approach the path of a learned person who has mastered their anger and remains self-controlled.
Good conduct brings greatness to everyone, so it should be protected more carefully than life itself.

Even if someone searches for and masters many other virtues, good conduct is the only true companion in life. Therefore, one should carefully protect and preserve this conduct, even through great hardship.
Good conduct is the true sign of a noble family, and bad conduct makes someone seem like they were born into a low family.
A person can regain forgotten knowledge by studying, but if they lose their good conduct, their high birth is destroyed.
Just as the envious person has no wealth, the person without good conduct has no greatness.
People with strong minds will not abandon proper conduct, because they know that doing so will bring disgrace and ruin to their family.
Good conduct brings people greatness, while bad conduct brings them undeserved disgrace.
Good conduct is the seed of blessings, while bad conduct always brings sorrow.
People with good character will not speak harmful words, even by accident.
Someone who has read many books but does not know how to live in harmony with the world and act according to the ways of good people is still ignorant.
The foolishness of lusting after someone else's wife does not exist in people who have studied and understood virtue and wealth.
Among all people who abandon virtue, there are no bigger fools than those who stand outside their neighbor's door lusting after his wife.
Someone who schemes to do evil to the wife of a person who trusts them is no different from a dead person.
No matter how great someone is, they lose all their greatness if they enter another person's wife without even thinking about their own guilt.
Someone who thinks it is easy to sleep with another man's wife and does so will acquire a permanent, undying stigma.
Someone who goes to another man's wife will never be rid of hatred, sin, fear, and disgrace.
A man who does not desire another man's wife is a righteous householder.
True manliness is looking at another person's wife without desire. For good people, this is not just a basic virtue, but the highest level of proper conduct.
In a world surrounded by the terrifying ocean, the people who are worthy of good things are those who do not touch the shoulder of someone who belongs to another.
Even if a person does not follow virtue and commits many sins, it is good if they do not desire another man's wife.
Bearing with those who revile you is the highest virtue, just as the earth bears up those who dig it.
It is good to always bear the harm done by others, but it is even better to forget it completely.
The worst form of poverty is turning away a guest without feeding them, and the greatest form of strength is tolerating the actions of ignorant fools.
If you want your great character to never leave you, you must practice and protect patience. A person who is a home of patience is praised by the world as a perfect human.
People will not value someone who seeks revenge, but they will treasure someone who patiently endures hardship as if it were gold.
The pleasure of someone who seeks revenge lasts only one day, while the praise of someone who is patient lasts until the world ends.
Even if someone else causes you pain, you should not do anything unjust in return. You should feel compassion for the suffering they will eventually face because of their bad actions.
One should overcome those who commit wrongs through pride by using one's own patience.
Those who patiently endure the harsh words of those who act without limits are as pure as ascetics.
Those who endure fasting are considered great, but those who endure harsh words from others are considered even greater.
A person should consider the habit of living without jealousy in their heart to be their moral standard. This means one should adopt a nature free from envy as their guiding rule of conduct.
Among all the great qualities a person can have, there is none better than not envying anyone. If someone can truly be free from envy towards others, then no other excellence can compare to it.
Someone who envies others' good fortune is said to not desire virtue or wealth for themselves.
Wise people do not commit unrighteous acts through envy because they know that such evil paths bring misery.
Someone who has envy does not need an enemy to destroy them, because their own envy is enough to cause their ruin.

Someone who envies the gifts given to others will cause their own family to perish without food or clothes. This envy brings ruin not only to the person who feels it, but also to their relatives who are left destitute.
Lakshmi, who brings wealth, will see a person who is envious of the prosperity of others, point him out to her older sister who brings poverty, and leave him.
Envy is an unmatched evil that destroys a person's wealth in this world and leads them into the fire of hell in the next.
People are surprised and deeply ponder why the life of someone with an envious heart flourishes while the life of a blameless person suffers.
No one who is envious becomes great, and no one who is free from envy fails to achieve greatness.
If someone covets another person's honest wealth without fairness, their family will be destroyed and they will incur guilt.
Someone who is ashamed of injustice will not commit shameful acts for the sake of gain.
Someone who desires the lasting happiness that comes from righteousness will not commit wrongful acts for the sake of fleeting, small pleasures.
People who have conquered their senses and are free from crime will not covet other people's wealth, even if they are experiencing poverty.
What is the use of vast knowledge if a person, driven by greed, acts foolishly towards everyone?
Someone who seeks grace and follows the righteous path will be destroyed if they desire wealth and think of evil deeds.
You should avoid the wealth gained by coveting other people's property, because the benefits of that wealth are not good when you actually enjoy them.
The way to keep wealth from decreasing is to not desire what belongs to someone else.
Good fortune comes to wise people who understand virtue and do not covet others' wealth. The goddess of wealth herself seeks out those who are worthy and approaches them at the right time.
Coveting another person's wealth without thinking of the consequences will bring destruction, but greatness of mind that does not desire that wealth will bring victory.
Even if someone does not talk about virtue and commits sins, it is good if people say that they do not backbite others.
Pretending to be friendly and smiling at someone to their face while secretly speaking evil about them behind their back is worse than openly rejecting virtue and committing sins.
It is better to die than to live by slandering people behind their backs and lying to their faces. Death brings the rewards promised by virtue, while living a deceitful life does not.
It is acceptable to speak harshly to someone's face, but you should not speak ill of them behind their back without considering the negative consequences.
Someone who praises virtue but slanders others behind their back does not truly have a virtuous mind. Their inner lack of virtue is revealed by their mean-spirited gossip.
Someone who points out the faults of others will have their own faults, especially the most severe ones, discovered and exposed by others.
Those who do not know how to make friends with pleasant words will, by speaking ill of others, cause even their friends to leave them.
Someone who habitually speaks ill of their close friends will surely do the same to strangers.
The earth tolerates the physical burden of people who speak bad words about others behind their backs, as if bearing their weight is a righteous duty.
If people observed their own faults as closely as they observe the faults of others, no harm would come to them.
Someone who speaks useless words that many people hate will be despised by everyone.
Speaking useless words in front of many people is worse than doing unkind things to friends.
When someone speaks at length about useless things, their words announce that they lack virtue and righteousness.
Speaking useless and unrefined words to a crowd will remove someone from goodness and virtue, and will not bring them any profit or pleasure.
When people of good character speak useless words, their glory and excellence will immediately leave them.
Do not call someone a human if they constantly speak useless words; you should call them chaff among people. Speaking useless words brings harm in both this life and the afterlife.
Wise people might speak harsh or unjust words, but it is better for them to avoid speaking useless words.
The wise who seek rare benefits will not speak words that lack great benefit.
People with pure, clear knowledge who are free from ignorance will never even by mistake speak useless words.
Speak words that are useful, and do not speak useless words.
Those who are used to doing evil deeds do not fear the pride of sin, but noble people do.
Since evil produces more evil, it should be feared more than fire.
The highest wisdom is to not do harm to those who hate you.
Even if you forget, you should not plot the ruin of another person, because virtue will surround and plot the ruin of anyone who does.
Do not commit evil deeds just because you are poor, because doing so will only make you poorer still.
Someone who does not want to suffer should not do harmful things to others.
Even if someone escapes every other enemy they have, the enmity of sin will relentlessly follow them and destroy them.
Destruction follows those who do evil, just as their shadow never leaves their feet.
If someone loves themselves, they should avoid committing even the smallest evil act against others.
A person who does not stray from the right path to commit evil deeds is free from harm and destruction.
Duty expects no return, just as the world does not repay the clouds for the rain. People who help others are like the rain, giving freely without expecting anything in return.
Wealth earned through hard work is meant to be used for helping those who are worthy or in need.
It is difficult to find a good deed equal to benevolence in the world of the gods and in this world.
Someone who knows how to help others truly lives, while someone who doesn't is considered as good as dead.

The wealth of a wise person who seeks the well-being of the world is like a village pond completely filled with water. This wealth is shared by everyone and never goes to waste, providing for the needs of all.
Wealth that is possessed by someone who is benevolent is like a fruitful tree in the middle of a town that has ripened with fruit.
If wealth is possessed by someone with a great and benevolent heart, it is like a tree that provides a cure for all illnesses, where every part of it can be used as medicine.
People who understand their duty will not stop being kind even when they have no money. They are the ones who know what they should do.
The poverty of a good person is their inability to help others, which makes them grieve because they cannot do the good deeds they want to do.
If a loss comes from doing good, that loss is worth buying even by selling yourself.
True charity is giving to the poor, while all other gifts are given with the expectation of a return.
It is wrong to beg even if people say it is a good path, and it is good to give even if people say it does not lead to heaven.
A person of noble birth gives to someone in need before they have to beg or say they have nothing. They give without letting the person feel humiliated, and they give consistently.
It is painful to see someone begging until you see their happy face after they have received what they asked for.
The strength of enduring one's own hunger is inferior to the strength of those who relieve the hunger of others.
Relieving the starving poor of their hunger is the place where a person who gains wealth can safely store it for future use.
A person who habitually shares their food with others will not be afflicted by the terrible disease of hunger.
Heartless people who hoard their wealth and eventually lose it do not know the joy of giving and seeing others happy.
Eating alone to fill one's own wealth is worse than begging.
Nothing is more painful than death, but it is even more painful to be unable to give to the poor.
Live a life of generous giving to the poor so that you gain great fame, because there is no greater reward for human life than that.
The praise of someone who gives alms to the poor is what everyone will speak about.
Nothing else in the world lasts forever except for exalted fame that has no equal.

If someone acquires lasting fame on earth, the world of the gods will praise them instead of the sages who reached that world. The gods will not praise the traditional sages if they can instead honor someone with enduring earthly fame.
Gaining wealth from poverty and gaining lasting fame from death are difficult to achieve for anyone other than the wise.
If you are born, be born with qualities that bring fame. For those without such qualities, it is better not to be born.
Why should someone who cannot live with fame be upset at those who despise them, instead of being upset with themselves for their own shortcomings?
If you do not leave behind a legacy of fame, people will call your life a disgrace.
The land that supports a body without fame will diminish in its rich produce.
Someone who lives without blame is truly living, while someone who lives without fame is not truly living.
The wealth of kindness is the greatest wealth, as even the lowest people possess material wealth.
Seek the good path and be compassionate, because even after exploring many different systems, compassion alone will be your aid.
People with merciful hearts do not enter the dark world of misery and hell.
A person who protects all living beings and shows them mercy will not have to fear any harm coming to their own soul.
People who are kind and merciful do not experience sorrow, and the vast, prosperous earth where the winds blow is a witness to this.
Those who abandon kindness and commit cruel acts are said to have lost their wealth and forgotten the suffering they will endure.

This world is not for those without wealth, just as the next world is not for those without kindness. Without wealth, a person cannot enjoy this world, and without kindness, they cannot enjoy the next world.
Someone who loses wealth can eventually regain it, but someone who loses grace is completely ruined and can never recover.
The good deeds of someone without kindness are like the true meaning of a text being understood by someone without wisdom.
When you are about to harm someone weaker than yourself, remember how you tremble in fear before those who are stronger than you.
How can someone who eats the flesh of other creatures to increase their own flesh be considered gracious?
Someone who does not protect their wealth has no use for it, just as someone who eats meat has no use for grace.
The mind of someone who eats the flesh of another creature is like the mind of someone who carries a weapon; it does not think of goodness or feel compassion.
Kindness is not killing, and killing is not kindness. Eating the flesh of a killed animal is a sin.
Not eating meat helps sustain life by sparing animals. If someone eats meat, hell swallows them and does not let them go.
If people did not kill living beings to eat their flesh, then no one would sell meat for money.
If people understood that eating meat is like eating the ulcer of another living being, they would stop eating it.
People whose minds are free from delusion do not eat meat that has been severed from a living being.
It is better not to kill and eat an animal's flesh than to pour a thousand offerings of ghee into a fire for sacrifices.
All living beings will join their hands in reverence to someone who does not kill any creature and refuses to eat meat.
True penance means enduring the hardships that come your way without causing pain to other living beings.
Austerities and spiritual discipline are only truly beneficial for those who have already practiced them in a previous life, so attempting them without that prior foundation is a useless effort.
Have other people forgotten to practice austerity in order to provide for the needs of ascetics?
Through the power of their austerities, someone can destroy their enemies and elevate their friends if they set their minds to it.

People practice religious discipline in this world because it allows them to attain exactly what they wish for in the afterlife. Because this practice guarantees that desires are fulfilled exactly as wished, wise people strive to perform it even while living a normal household life.
Those who perform austerities are the ones who do their duty, while others, entangled in desire, engage in futile actions.
Just as gold becomes brighter when heated in a fire, those who endure pain become more enlightened. The more they suffer, the more their wisdom grows.
Someone who has gained control over their own soul will be worshipped by all other living beings. This is because they have given up the attachment to their own self and the pride of being someone.
Those who gain power through religious discipline can even conquer death.
Because there are few people who practice austerity and many who do not, many people in the world are poor while few are rich.

A hypocrite who pretends to be a good person will eventually be exposed by the five elements inside his own body. These elements, which make up his physical form, will laugh among themselves at his hidden bad conduct because his sins cannot stay hidden forever.
What good is a reputation for being very holy if your own conscience knows you have done wrong?
Pretending to be a powerful ascetic while lacking the self-control to master one's mind is like a cow wearing a tiger's skin to graze on the crops.
Pretending to be a holy person while doing evil deeds is like a hunter hiding in the bushes to catch birds.
Those who pretend to be free from attachment but secretly act wrongly will later suffer many sorrows and cry out, "What have we done.
There is no one more cruel than a person who lives by cheating others while pretending to be a saint, even though they have not truly given up their inner desires.
Some people in the world look as bright red as the outside of the kunri berry, but their minds are as black as the inside of its nose.

There are many people who hide their inner impurity and sins behind a show of bathing in water or acting like noble people. They pretend to be pure and virtuous on the outside while remaining polluted and deceitful on the inside.
A straight arrow is cruel, while a curved lute is sweet. Judge people by their actions, not by their appearance.
There is no point in shaving your head or growing your hair long if you stop doing the things that people condemn.
Someone who wants to live without being despised by others should protect their mind from even the thought of stealing or cheating others out of any possession.
Even thinking about stealing someone else's wealth through fraud is a sin. Therefore, you should not even conceive of deceitfully taking another person's property.
Wealth acquired through fraud might seem to grow beyond all limits, but it will quickly be destroyed. It destroys the wealth you already had, taking it away along with the ill-gotten gains.
A strong desire to cheat others out of their wealth will, when it bears fruit, cause undying sorrow.
Someone who watches for others to be careless in order to steal their wealth does not possess grace and love. They do not value grace, nor do they practice kindness or love.
People who are intensely greedy to steal others' wealth cannot live a life of moderation and restraint.
People who desire to live with measured wisdom do not have the dark knowledge of fraud.
Virtue resides in the hearts of those who understand righteousness, while deceit resides in the hearts of those who understand fraud.
Those who know nothing but theft will perish while committing their crimes.

Even the body rejects thieves, while heaven does not reject those who are free from fraud. Those who steal lose even their lives in this world, but those who do not steal will certainly attain the world of the gods.
Truth is speaking words that do not cause any harm to anyone.
Even falsehood can be considered truth if it brings a faultless benefit to others.
A person should not lie about something that their own heart knows is true, because once the lie is told, their own mind will punish them with guilt and sorrow.
Someone who lives without any deceit in their heart will dwell in the hearts of all people.
Speaking the truth sincerely from the heart is better than giving gifts and practicing austerities.
There is no praise like the praise of never lying, and this truthfulness itself gives all virtues without the person even realizing it.

If someone can truly live without ever lying, it is good even if they do not practice any other virtues. If a person can abstain from falsehood, it will be well with them even if they leave other virtuous acts undone.
Water makes the body pure, and truth makes the mind pure.

Not all lights are true lights for the wise; only the light of truth is a true light. Physical lamps only remove external darkness, but the light of truth removes inner darkness, making it the only real lamp for wise people.
Among all the good things we have seen in the scriptures, there is nothing better than truthfulness.
Someone who does not get angry when they can harm someone is truly self-controlled. When they cannot harm someone, what does it matter if they restrain their anger or not?
Being angry at people who have no power to hurt you is harmful to yourself, but being angry at people who actually have the power to hurt you is an even worse evil.
You should forget the anger you feel towards anyone, because anger is the source of all evil.
Anger is a greater enemy than any other foe because it kills both the smile on the face and the joy in the heart.
To protect yourself, you must guard against anger, because if you do not, anger will destroy you.
The fire of anger will burn up even the helpful raft of friendship.
Someone who treats anger as a source of strength will face ruin, just as a hand that strikes the ground cannot avoid feeling the pain.
Even if someone causes you pain as severe as being burned by a massive fire, it is best to avoid getting angry at them if you possibly can.
If a person does not think of anger in their heart, they will immediately obtain everything they have thought of.
Someone who has excessive anger is like a dead person, but someone who completely gives up anger is like someone who has given up everything.
Even if they could obtain wealth that brings greatness by causing harm to others, the principle of the pure is to never cause pain to anyone.
Someone who gets angry and harms you should not be harmed in return, because the spotless do not do evil even to those who have done them evil.
If you retaliate and cause harm to people who hate you even though you have done them no harm, that action will bring you unavoidable and inescapable suffering.
The best way to punish someone who has harmed you is to do them a kindness, which will shame them, and then forget both the harm they did and any good you have done.
What benefit is there in being wise if you do not protect others from pain as you would your own?
If you have personally experienced something as painful, you should not do it to someone else. You should avoid doing to others the things that you know will cause them sorrow.
It is the highest virtue not to cause harm to anyone, even in the smallest way, at any time, or even in thought.
If someone knows through their own experience how painful it is to be harmed, why would they ever harm another living being?
If you harm others in the morning, the same harm will come to you in the evening.
Evils return to the one who causes them, so people who want to be free from sorrow will not harm others.
Virtue is simply not killing any living being, because killing causes every kind of evil.
Sharing food with others and protecting all living beings is the most important virtue among all those taught in the scriptures.
Not killing is the greatest good, and next to it is not speaking falsehood.
The good path is the one that avoids killing any living being.
Among all those who renounce worldly life out of a fear of the cycle of birth and death, the greatest is the one who fears the sin of murder and strictly avoids killing.

Death will not take the life of someone who has made a vow never to kill. By practicing the vow of non-violence, a person will live out their full lifespan, and even the life-eating god of death will not interfere.
Even if you must lose your own life, you should not kill another person to save yourself.
Even if killing in a sacrifice brings great gain, the wise consider the gain from killing to be dishonorable.
People who make a living by killing are considered to be eating carrion by those who know what is vile. Even if they do not realize their own degradation, wise people view them as lowly and base.
Wise people say that those who suffer from poverty and disease while living a miserable life are people who killed animals in their past lives by taking their lives away from their bodies.
Thinking that impermanent things are permanent is a foolish and degrading state of mind.
Wealth gathers like a crowd coming to watch a play, and it disappears like the crowd leaving when the play ends.
Wealth is fleeting, so as soon as you acquire it, you should use it to do enduring good deeds.
Time, which appears as a day, is actually a saw that cuts away life. Only someone who understands this knows it to be so.
Do good deeds quickly before you lose control of your tongue and your breathing becomes heavy and gurgling.
This world has the greatness of being able to say that someone who existed yesterday is not today.
Someone who does not know if they will live another moment will think of countless things.
The soul's friendship with the body is like a bird leaving its egg and flying away.
Death is like falling into a deep sleep, and birth is like waking up from it. These two events naturally alternate with each other, just like sleeping and waking.

The soul that resides in this body, which is a temporary shelter for diseases, has not yet found a permanent home. Since the soul is merely a lodger in this fragile body and will eventually depart, it has not yet attained a stable, lasting resting place.
A person does not suffer pain from whatever thing they have detached themselves from.
If you want to be free from suffering, you must renounce everything while you still have it. After renouncing, you can enjoy many pleasures in this world.
One must control the five senses and their desires, and at the same time, let go of everything one has desired.
Being completely without possessions is the natural state for those who perform austerities. Owning anything, even one thing, will cause them to become confused again.
Even the physical body is a heavy burden for those trying to cut off future births, so why should they add even more attachments?

Someone who destroys the pride of saying "I" and "mine" will attain a high world that is difficult even for the gods to reach. They will do this by removing the ignorance of considering the body as "I" and unrelated objects as "mine".
Those who do not let go of their attachments will never be let go by grief.
Those who have completely renounced everything attain the highest state, while those who do not renounce are deluded and trapped in the net of birth.
When a person lets go of all attachments, rebirth is cut off. If they do not let go of attachments, the cycle of birth and death will continue.
Bind yourself to the one who is without attachments, and by doing so, you will break all your other attachments.
Confusing things that are not real with things that are real leads to a miserable birth. This delusion is the primary cause of suffering in rebirth.
For those who have a pure vision free from delusion, darkness departs and they experience delight. This pure vision removes ignorance and grants the happiness of liberation.

For people whose minds are clear and free from doubt, the heaven they should attain is much closer than the earth they live on. When they resolve their doubts through clear reasoning, the spiritual world they desire feels much nearer than the physical world, and they gain the confidence that they can reach it.
Even if someone has fully mastered their five senses and their mind, it is useless to them if they do not know the true nature of reality.
True knowledge is seeing the real nature of a thing, regardless of how it appears.
Those who learn and realize the true nature of reality in this lifetime will attain the path of no return, meaning they will not be born into this world again.

Someone who thoroughly examines and firmly understands the true meaning of what they have been taught does not need to worry about taking another birth. If a person's mind deeply contemplates and clearly realizes the inner truth, they should not think that rebirth will happen to them.
True knowledge is to see the supreme truth and remove the folly of birth, which is caused by ignorance. This wisdom is the cause of liberation from the suffering of rebirth.
If someone understands the ultimate reality and lives without attachment, the suffering that once clung to them will be destroyed and will not return.
If the very names of desire, anger, and delusion are destroyed, then the diseases and sorrows they cause will also disappear.
Desire is the seed that causes endless birth for all living things at all times.
If you desire anything, you should desire freedom from birth. That freedom from birth will come if you desire to be without desire.
There is no wealth in this world or any other that is equal to the wealth of not wanting anything.

True purity is the absence of desires, and this state is attained by those who seek the truth. The absence of desires is the result of seeking the truth, because those who do not crave anything will not tell lies.
Those who are free from desire are truly free, while others are not free even if they are free from other things.
Desire is what deceives and destroys a person, so living with fear of desire is virtue.
If a person completely eliminates desire, they will achieve immortal deeds in the path they choose.
There is no sorrow for those without desire, but where desire exists, sorrow comes endlessly and without end.
If the greatest sorrow, which is desire, is destroyed, then joy will never cease.
If someone gets rid of an insatiable desire that is never fulfilled, that very state will give them a permanent, unchanging blissful nature.
When fate brings wealth, effort follows; when fate brings loss, laziness follows.
A fate that causes loss makes a person foolish, while a fate that brings gain expands their knowledge.
Even if someone studies many subtle texts, their innate wisdom will still prevail.
Through fate, the world has two different natures, which is why some people gain wealth while others attain wisdom.
When trying to make wealth, fate causes good things to turn bad and bad things to turn good.
Things not meant for you will not stay with you no matter how carefully you guard them, and things that are meant for you will not leave you even if you throw them away.
Even those who gather millions can only enjoy them according to what has been determined by the disposer of all things.
If the poor are spared from the suffering that fate usually brings them, they will give up their desires and become ascetics.
People who are happy when good things happen should not be sad when bad things happen, since both are just part of life.
What power is stronger than fate? Even if you try to find a way to avoid it, fate will get there first.
A king who possesses an army, a loyal population, wealth, a minister, allies, and a fort is a lion among kings.
A king should never lack courage, generosity, wisdom, and energy.
A ruler must always have alertness, learning, and bravery. These three qualities are essential for someone who governs a country.
A king who never strays from virtue and never commits vice, and who is never without courage and honor, is the best ruler.
A capable king is someone who creates ways to earn wealth, accumulates it, protects it from being stolen by others, and spends it on righteousness, prosperity, and happiness.
The world will praise the land of a king who is easy to see and does not speak harsh words. A kingdom expands when the ruler is easy to approach and never uses harsh language.

A ruler who speaks pleasantly and gives to others, while also protecting them, will have the whole world praise him and obey his commands. The world will submit to the king who can give generously with sweet words and protect everyone who comes to him.
A king who performs his duties properly and protects his people will be considered a god by them.
A king who can endure harsh words will have the whole world living under his protection.
A king who has generosity, grace, just rule, and care for the weak is a guiding light for all other kings.
Learn whatever you study without any mistakes, and then live your life in a way that is worthy of what you have learned.
Letters and numbers are the two eyes of all living beings.
The learned are said to have eyes, while the ignorant have two sores on their face.
The learned should meet people in a way that brings them joy and leave in a way that makes them think of the next meeting. This is the art of a scholar.
The unlearned stand in a low position before the learned, just as the poor stand before the rich. Those who do not learn are considered inferior.
The deeper you dig a sandy well, the more water flows out, and similarly, the more a person learns, the more knowledge they gain.
A learned person can treat any country as their own and any town as their home, so why does someone spend their life until death without learning anything?
The knowledge a person learns in a single lifetime will help them for seven lifetimes.
Learned people will want to learn more when they see that their knowledge brings pleasure to both themselves and the world.
Learning is the best wealth that cannot be destroyed; nothing else is true wealth.
Speaking in a gathering without having studied the books that give full knowledge is like playing checkers without drawing a board.
An uneducated person wanting to speak in an assembly is like a woman without breasts desiring womanhood.
Someone who is uneducated is considered a very good person if they remain silent in the presence of the learned.
Even if an uneducated person has excellent natural knowledge, a wise person will not accept it as true knowledge.
An unlearned person's pride disappears when they speak in front of knowledgeable people.
Unlearned people are said to exist, but they are like barren land that yields nothing because they are of no use to themselves or to others.

The beauty and greatness of a person who lacks deep, extensive knowledge are like the appearance of a beautifully decorated clay doll. Such a person has no real substance, and their outward charm is entirely worthless.
Wealth in the hands of the unlearned causes more suffering than the poverty of the learned.
An uneducated person, even if born into a high caste, does not have the same dignity as an educated person, even if the educated person was born into a low caste.

Compared to people, animals are inferior, and compared to those who have studied great books, uneducated people are just as inferior. The difference between educated people and those who have not studied is exactly the same as the difference between humans and animals.
The wealth of wealth is the wealth gained through listening, and this wealth is the best of all wealth.

When there is no food for the ear, give a little food to the stomach as well. If the stomach is very hungry, it will not care about the lack of intellectual food, so you should still provide a little to eat.
Someone who feeds their ears with good questions is equal to the gods who eat the food offered in sacrifices.
Even if someone is uneducated, they should listen to the teachings of the learned, because doing so provides a helpful support during times of weakness or adversity.
The words of a virtuous person are like a staff that helps you walk on slippery ground.
Listening to good things, even a little, will bring great dignity.

Someone who has deeply studied and carefully listened to learn the truth will not speak foolishly, even if they have made a mistake. Even when they realize they have imperfectly understood something, they will not say ignorant things.
An ear that has not been opened by instruction is deaf, even if it hears sound.
It is hard for someone who has not heard refined knowledge to speak modest words. People who lack this understanding are unlikely to have a humble mouth.

People who only experience the physical tastes of the mouth and cannot appreciate the aesthetic and emotional tastes heard through the ear have nothing to lose if they die, and nothing to gain if they live.
Wisdom is a weapon that prevents destruction and an inner fortress that enemies cannot destroy.
Wisdom prevents the mind from wandering wherever it wants to go, removes evil, and guides it toward the good.

True wisdom is the ability to discern the actual truth of a matter, regardless of who speaks it or where you hear it. One should not blindly accept what anyone says, but should instead carefully analyze it to find out what is actually true.
Wisdom is the ability to speak clearly and simply so that others easily understand your thoughts, and to carefully figure out the subtle meanings hidden in the words of others.
True wisdom is to befriend the great and remain steadfast in that friendship, not opening and closing like a lotus flower.

A wise person adapts their behavior to match how the world operates. The classical commentaries explain that this means living in harmony with the world and the great people in it, rather than stubbornly trying to force the world to conform to one's own ways.
The wise can foresee what will happen in the future, while the unwise cannot.
It is foolishness to not fear what should be feared, and it is the duty of the wise to fear what should be feared.
People with the wisdom to foresee and guard against future troubles will not suffer terrifying or shocking misfortunes.
Those who have wisdom have everything, and those who do not have wisdom have nothing, even if they possess things.
True greatness belongs to those who are free from pride, anger, and lust. Their prosperity is the most valuable and enduring.
A king commits a fault when he is greedy, has undignified pride, and finds joy in bad things.
People who fear disgrace will consider a fault as small as a millet seed to be as large as a palmyra tree, and will avoid committing it.
A fault is a deadly enemy that destroys you, so you should protect yourself by guarding against it as if it were your most valuable treasure.
Someone who does not guard against a fault before it arrives will lose their life like straw placed before a fire.
A king who first corrects his own faults and then examines the faults of others has no fault.
The wealth of a stingy person who does not spend it on good deeds will be wasted and destroyed.
The greed of a miser's heart is not counted as one fault among others; it is the worst of all faults.
One should never boast about oneself or desire to do things that do not yield any benefit.
If someone can secretly enjoy the things they love without others knowing about it, the plans of their enemies will fail.

chapter: Seeking the Aid of Great Men
modern: It is ten times worse to abandon the friendship of good people than to incur the hatred of many enemies.
Noble people fear the company of the base, but low-minded people embrace them as friends.
The nature of water changes according to the soil it flows through, and a person's wisdom changes according to the character of their associates.
A person's character comes from their mind, but how they are judged by others comes from the people they associate with.
Wisdom seems to come from the mind, but it actually comes from the company a person keeps.
Purity of mind and purity of action both come from having pure company.
A pure mind leads to good descendants and fame, while a pure lineage ensures that no bad deeds are done.
Goodness of mind brings wealth, and good companionship brings all praise.
Even if a wise person already has great mental goodness, the good company of friends will further protect and strengthen it.
Goodness of mind brings future bliss, and this is strengthened by the company of good people.
There is no greater help than the company of the good, and no greater source of sorrow than the company of the wicked.

Before doing an action, a person should figure out what will be lost, what will be gained, and what the future reward will be, and then act. They should weigh the loss, the gain, and the reward of a deed before proceeding to do it.
There is nothing difficult to achieve for someone who carefully plans an action with trusted friends and then reflects on it themselves before doing it.
Wise people do not undertake actions that risk losing their current capital just to gain more profit.
Someone who fears being blamed will not start a task whose outcome is not clear.
Going to war without thoroughly considering all the ways to act and the resulting outcomes is a way to plant an enemy in growing soil so he can thrive.
Doing what is not fit to do causes ruin, and not doing what is fit to do also causes ruin.
A person should think and plan before starting a proper task, and it is wrong to say they will think about it after they have already started.
Effort without a proper method will fail, even if many people support it.
Even when trying to do good, mistakes happen if you do not understand people's individual natures and act accordingly.
A person should plan and perform actions that others will not despise, because the world will reject and mock actions that do not suit their status or position.
One should weigh the strength of the task, one's own strength, the enemy's strength, and the strength of allies before acting.
People who know their own strength and figure out exactly what they need to do before taking action will never face an impossible task.
Many people, ignorant of their own strength, start a task with great enthusiasm but fail and are destroyed in the middle of it.
Someone who does not get along with others and does not know their own strength will quickly be destroyed.

Even if you load a cart with light peacock feathers, the axle will break if you overload it beyond its capacity. This means that even if you are strong, you will be destroyed if you make too many enemies beyond your capacity to handle them.
Someone who climbs to the very tip of a branch and then tries to go further will lose their life. This is a warning against overreaching one's limits.
A person should give to others only up to the limit of their ability, and giving in this measured way is the proper way to preserve their wealth.
Even if income is small, there is no harm as long as spending is not excessive.
A person who does not know the limits of their wealth and lives beyond their means will eventually lose everything, even if their life initially seems prosperous.
Giving without considering one's own wealth will quickly destroy that wealth.
A crow can defeat an owl in broad daylight, so a king who wants to defeat his enemies must choose the right time to fight.
Acting according to the right season is a cord that binds success so it does not slip away.
Is there anything difficult for someone who acts with the right tools at the right time?
If you act at the right time and place, you can easily win even the whole world, even if that is your greatest ambition.
Someone who wants to conquer the world waits patiently and without anxiety for the right time to act.

A powerful person waits for the right moment to act instead of attacking immediately, just as a fighting ram steps back to gather momentum before charging its enemy. This self-restraint is not due to fear, but a deliberate pause to build strength for a more effective strike.
The wise do not show their anger outwardly when someone harms them, but instead wait for the right time to act and keep their anger hidden inside.
If you see your enemy, bear with them patiently until their time of destruction arrives, and then their head will fall.
When a rare and perfect opportunity arises, one should immediately perform the hardest deeds.
Wait patiently like a heron when the time is not right, and strike decisively like its peck when the time is right.
Do not start any action or despise your enemy until you have found a suitable place to completely surround them.
Even for those who are powerful and skilled in warfare, gaining an advantage by using a fortress will bring many benefits.
Even the weak can win if they choose the right place, protect themselves, and attack their enemies.
If someone chooses a good position to fight from, their enemies will lose the confidence they had in winning.
A crocodile prevails over other animals in deep water, but if it leaves the water, other animals will defeat it.
Large chariots with strong wheels cannot run on the ocean, and ships that sail on the sea cannot run on land. One should choose the right tools for the right place.
If you carefully plan your actions and choose the right place to do them, you will not need any help other than fearlessness.

If a king with a large army attacks a smaller army in a place where only the smaller army can operate, the large army's morale and strength will be destroyed. Even a smaller army can defeat a larger one if it fights from a location that favors its size.
It is difficult to attack people in their own land, even if they have no fort or other strengths.
A fox can kill a fearless elephant with a warrior's face if the elephant gets stuck in deep mud where its legs sink.

A person's true character should be tested through their virtue, wealth, pleasure, and fear of death before they are chosen for a job. You should observe how they behave regarding morality, money, physical pleasure, and their own life to understand their true nature.

Someone born into a good family, free from faults, and who feels shame at the thought of doing wrong is the one a king should trust. This person is of noble birth, has no faults, and is modest enough to fear the wounds of sin.
Even deeply learned and faultless people are rarely found to be completely free of ignorance when examined closely.
Weigh a person's good qualities and faults, and judge them based on whichever is more abundant.
A person's own actions are the true test for determining their greatness and their meanness.
Do not choose people who have no family or relatives, because they have no worldly attachments and feel no shame in committing bad deeds.

Choosing ignorant people for a position out of personal affection brings all kinds of ignorance and useless outcomes. This happens because the king or leader, relying on affection rather than knowledge, appoints the wrong people, leading to ignorance and failure.
Trusting an untried stranger without examining their character and background causes endless, inescapable troubles for a person and their descendants.
Do not trust anyone without thoroughly testing them, and once they are tested, confidently entrust them with suitable duties.
Trusting someone without examining them and doubting someone after you have examined and trusted them both cause endless sorrow.
Someone who naturally chooses the good after weighing both good and evil should be employed.
A ruler should act to expand sources of wealth, increase prosperity, and identify and remove any obstacles that threaten it.
You should trust someone who has a strong love for their work, the knowledge to do it well, the confidence to carry it out, and a lack of greed for the rewards.
Even after being carefully examined and found suitable in every possible way, many people still change their minds or act differently when it is time to actually perform the task.
One should not assign a task to someone just because they are a favorite, but only to a person who knows how to do it and can handle any difficulties that arise.
One should carefully consider the qualifications of the person who will do the work, the nature of the task itself, and the right time to do it, and then proceed with the action.
After considering that this man can accomplish this work with these means, one should leave that task with him.
After finding out what work a person is suited for, assign them to that specific job. Once appointed, let them perform the tasks that match their abilities.
Wealth and prosperity will leave a king who doubts the friendship of a man who is always diligent in his duties.
A king must daily examine the actions of his servants, because if they do not act crookedly, the world will not act crookedly.
Even when a person has lost all their wealth, only relatives will continue to show them their old kindness and maintain their relationship.
If a person has relatives who love them without fail, that will give them ever-increasing wealth.
The life of someone who does not mingle with relatives is like water filling a tank with no banks.
The benefit of acquiring wealth is living surrounded by relatives who are happy and close to you.
Someone who gives what is needed and speaks kindly will be surrounded by many relatives.
A person who gives generously and does not get angry will have more relatives than anyone else in the world.
When crows find food, they do not hide it but call their relatives to share it with them; similarly, wealth and good fortune belong only to those who share their wealth with their relatives.
When a king looks at people based on their individual merits instead of treating everyone the same, many relatives will stay close to him.
People who were once close friends but left for a specific reason will return and stay with him once that cause is gone.
When someone who left without a reason comes back with a specific motive, the king should fulfill that purpose, examine their intentions, and accept them back.
Forgetting oneself in great joy is worse than excessive anger.
Forgetting destroys fame just as constant poverty destroys knowledge.
Thoughtless people cannot gain fame, and this is a conclusion accepted by all schools of thought.
Someone who is fearful finds no use in any fortress, just as someone who is forgetful finds no good in any high position.
A person who fails to foresee and guard against future troubles will later regret his mistake.
There is no greater benefit than always maintaining an unfailing, unforgetting nature towards everyone.
There is nothing too difficult to accomplish if you work carefully with an unfailing, unforgetting mind.
One should carefully perform actions that the wise praise. Anyone who ignores and fails to do them will find no happiness in any of their seven births.
When you are overwhelmed by joy, remember the people who were ruined in the past because of their own arrogance and neglect.
It is easy to get what you want if you can keep thinking about it without forgetting.
To investigate a crime without showing favoritism to anyone, and then to decide and carry out the appropriate punishment based on the law.

All living creatures on earth depend on the rain to survive, and in the same way, the subjects depend on the king's just rule. If the rain fails, the creatures cannot live, and if the king's justice fails, the subjects cannot thrive.
A king's rule is the foundation for the Vedas and the virtues described by Brahmins, and it protects the world.

A ruler who governs his land with love and embraces his subjects will have the world constantly clinging to his feet. People will live by following the path of a good ruler who governs his people fairly and holds them close.
In a country ruled by a king who governs justly according to the scriptures, timely rains and abundant crops will always occur together.

It is not the spear but the king's straight scepter that brings victory, provided that scepter does not do injustice. A ruler's victory comes from just governance rather than weapons, as long as their rule remains fair and does not oppress the people.
The king protects the entire earth, and justice protects him as long as he rules without making mistakes.

A king who is hard of access to those seeking justice, does not investigate their complaints thoroughly, and rules without proper justice will ruin himself. He will fall into a lowly state and perish even without any enemies.
A king's duty is to protect his subjects from harm, preserve them himself, and punish any wrongdoing without fearing blame.
When a king executes cruel people to protect the good, it is like a farmer pulling up weeds to save the crops.
A king who oppresses his subjects is more cruel than a murderer.
A king who stands with a sceptre and asks his subjects for money is just like a highway robber who stands with a weapon and demands your wealth.
A king who does not daily investigate wrongs and administer justice will see his kingdom fall into ruin day by day.
A king who rules without thinking about the consequences will lose both his wealth and his subjects.
The tears shed by people suffering under an unjust ruler and crying out in unbearable pain act as a tool that wears away and destroys the ruler's wealth.
Righteous rule is what makes a king's fame last; without it, the king's fame will not endure.
A king who lacks kindness causes the same kind of suffering to his living subjects as a lack of rain causes to the world.

Being wealthy is more painful than being poor if you live under the rule of an unjust king. The sorrow of possessing wealth is worse than the sorrow of lacking it when living beneath a cruel, unjust ruler.
If a king rules unjustly, the seasons will change and the sky will not provide rain.

If the king fails to properly protect the country, the cows will give less milk and the Brahmins will forget their sacred texts. Without protection, the cows lose their milk yield, and the people who perform the six Vedic duties stop reciting the mantras, so sacrifices no longer take place.
A king is someone who investigates a crime fairly and then punishes the offender in a way that prevents them from committing the same crime again.

To ensure long-lasting rule, a ruler should begin punishments with a show of severity but then carry them out with gentleness. This approach prevents fear and ensures the ruler's authority remains strong over time.
If a fierce king rules by doing cruel deeds that make his subjects fear him, the king will certainly and quickly come to ruin.
A king who is called cruel by his subjects will quickly lose his life and wealth.

The great wealth of someone who is difficult to see and has a harsh face is ruined by the evil gaze of a demon. Because such a person is unapproachable and unpleasant to look at, their wealth is wasted and serves no use to themselves or to others.
The wealth of a ruler who is harsh in speech and unkind in appearance will quickly perish.
Harsh words and excessive punishments wear away a king's strength to defeat his enemies.
