A weapon can be hidden in the very hands of enemies who bow to you, and their tears are just as deceptive.
When enemies outwardly show great friendship but inwardly despise you, you should pretend to be friendly with them and make them outwardly happy so that their inner hatred fades away.
When your enemies pretend to be friends, you should smile at them but not trust them in your heart. If they later become truly friendly, you should also give up that friendship.
Folly is the choice to accept things that bring harm while letting go of things that bring gain. It is the act of choosing loss over profit and harm over good.
The greatest folly is to take delight in doing what is forbidden.
Shamelessness, aimlessness, lovelessness, and not cherishing anything are the qualities of a fool.
There is no greater fool than someone who reads and understands teachings, explains them to others, but does not follow them himself.
A foolish person who acts alone in a single lifetime can create a hell for themselves, into which they will sink and suffer across all seven future births.
When a fool who doesn't know the right way starts a task, not only does the task fail, but he also gets into trouble.
When a foolish person acquires great wealth, strangers and neighbors feast on it while his own relatives starve.
When a fool gets something, he is like a person who is already drunk and then drinks more alcohol.
Friendship with fools is very pleasant because parting from them does not bring any sorrow.
A fool entering a gathering of wise people is like placing unwashed feet on a bed.
The lack of wisdom is the greatest of all lacks, but the world does not consider the lack of wealth to be a lack at all.
When a fool gives something with a happy heart, it is only because the receiver has good karma from a past life.
Fools inflict a kind of suffering on themselves that even their enemies would not.
Stupidity is the arrogance of thinking you are wise.
Someone who pretends to know what they have not learned will cause others to doubt even what they actually do know.
Fools try to hide their nakedness with clothes while failing to cover their inner faults. Trying to hide one's body is foolish if one does not first remove one's faults.
A fool who neglects sacred teachings brings great harm upon himself.
Someone who does not do good things even when advised and does not understand them on their own is a plague to the world until they die.
Someone who tries to teach a foolish person who lacks knowledge will be considered ignorant himself, while the foolish person will just think he is wise based on the little he knows.
Someone who denies the existence of things that wise and good people clearly affirm, even when proven by evidence, will be considered a demon or ghost on earth.
Hatred is a disease that creates a lack of harmony among all living beings and fosters the bad quality of disunion.
Even if someone who is not on your side does hateful things, it is better not to do hateful things back to them.
If a person removes the painful disease of hatred from their mind, it will give them imperishable and lasting fame.
If hatred, which is the greatest misery, is destroyed, it will yield the greatest delight.
No one can defeat people who do not hold onto anger or hatred. They are the ones who cannot be conquered.
The life of someone who thinks it is sweet to have enmity with others is near failure and ruin. Their life is also near poverty and death.
People who have a hateful mind cannot understand the truth that leads to victory.
Turning away from enmity is a gain, but actively encouraging it brings fast ruin.
When good fortune arrives, a person does not think of hatred, but when they are seeking their own ruin, they will think of increasing it.
All evils come from enmity, and all goodness comes from friendship.
Avoid fighting against those who are stronger than you, but actively seek out enmity with those who are weaker.
Someone who has no love for his relatives, lacks powerful allies, and has no strength of his own cannot defeat a strong enemy.
Someone who is timid, ignorant, unsociable, and stingy is very easy for enemies to defeat.
Someone who does not let go of their anger and cannot keep secrets will always and everywhere be an easy target for anyone.
Someone who does not follow the right path, does not do what is appropriate, does not fear blame, and lacks good qualities is easily defeated by his enemies.

It is actually good to be hated by someone who is blinded by anger and whose lust keeps growing. People will gladly accept the enmity of a person who acts without thinking and is consumed by endless desire.

If someone who started a task does things that ruin it, you must secure their enmity even if it costs you some wealth. You should not hesitate to pay a price to make an enemy of someone who acts against the good of a shared endeavor.
A person who lacks good qualities and has many faults will lose their friends and supporters. This loss of support only strengthens and delights their enemies.
The joy of victory is endless when the enemy is both ignorant and timid.
Someone who avoids fighting an unlearned person will never gain fame.
No one should desire or practice the evil of enmity, not even as a joke or for fun.
You can make enemies with warriors who use bows, but you should not make enemies with scholars who use words.
Someone who is alone and makes many enemies is more foolish than even a mad person.
The world depends on the greatness of a good-natured ruler who turns his enemies into friends. The world remains secure under his capable and powerful rule.
If someone is alone and has no allies against two enemies, they should make one of those enemies a friendly ally.
Whether you trust your enemy or not, during a time of disaster, you should neither join them nor separate from them.
Do not tell your pain to people who are unaware of it, and do not show your weakness to your enemies.
By knowing how to act, strengthening yourself, and seeking protection, the pride and joy of your enemies will naturally be destroyed.
You should destroy your enemies when they are weak, because when they become strong, they will destroy you.

Someone who does not crush the pride of their enemies will not even survive long enough to breathe. Those who fail to destroy the arrogance of those who hate them will surely be killed by their enemies before they can even take a breath.
Water and shade are good only if they don't cause harm, and relatives are good only if they don't cause harm.
You do not need to fear enemies who are openly hostile like drawn swords, but you should fear the friendship of enemies who pretend to be allies.
One should guard against internal enemies, as they will inevitably destroy you during a time of weakness just like a tool that cuts a potter's clay.
If a person harbors secret inner hostility, it causes many evils and makes their own relatives turn against them.
If hidden hatred arises among close relatives, it will cause many fatal harms and crimes.
If hatred arises among one's own people, it is always hard to escape death. If discord finds a place among those who lived together in unity, it is ever hard to keep destruction away.
A family with internal hatred cannot truly unite, even if it appears united on the outside like a lid on a box.
A household with internal hatred loses its strength like iron being worn down by a file.
Even if internal hatred is as small as a split in a sesame seed, it contains the potential for great destruction.
Living with people who are not in agreement with you is like dwelling in a hut with a snake.
It is the best protection to not despise the power of those who can successfully complete their actions. This is better than all the other safeguards people use to protect themselves from harm.
If you do not respect powerful people, they will cause you endless suffering.
If you want to ruin yourself, do not listen to the advice of the righteous and commit crimes against those who are powerful enough to destroy other kings.
When powerless people do evil to those who have power, they are like beckoning Death with their own hands to come and destroy them.
Someone who has angered a powerful ruler cannot survive anywhere they go.
Someone who is burned by fire might still survive, but a person who offends the great will not survive.
If great and worthy people become angry, all the king's wealth and luxurious life are useless.
If people try to ruin those who are as great as a mountain, even those who seem to be permanently established on earth, along with their families, will be completely destroyed.
If someone of high principles gets angry, even a king will lose his position and be ruined.
Even someone with massive wealth and powerful allies will not survive if they face the anger of highly virtuous and noble people.

Someone who is deeply infatuated with their wife and acts exactly as she says will not attain the great benefits of virtue. This kind of pleasure is also rejected by those who are focused on achieving wealth and taking action.

A man who abandons his own masculinity to obsessively dote on his wife will bring great shame upon himself and all other men. His wealth will be wasted on her, and he will be left feeling deeply ashamed of his loss of manhood.
A man who is submissive to his wife will always feel ashamed when he is among good people.
A man who fears his wife will not gain salvation, and his actions will not be praised.
Someone who fears his wife will always be afraid to do good deeds, even for good people.
Someone who fears their wife's slender arm will have no dignity, even if they live like gods.
A woman who has a sense of shame is more honorable than a man who simply obeys her commands.
Someone who follows their wife's wishes will not help their friends in need or do good deeds.
People who obey their wives' commands will not achieve virtuous deeds, wealth, or pleasure.

Someone who is intelligent and wealthy will never act foolishly by blindly obeying their wife's orders. People with a strong and thoughtful mind do not fall into the foolishness of being completely devoted to a woman.
The sweet words of women who seek a man's wealth rather than his love will ultimately cause him sorrow.
Do not associate with women who feign virtue to gain wealth, as they are ill-natured.
The false embrace of women who only want money is like someone in a dark room hugging a dead body they don't know.
People who seek the wealth of grace will not desire the low pleasures of prostitutes who only care about money.
People with excellent, naturally good minds will not desire the cheap physical charms of women who offer their favors to anyone who pays them.
Wise people who want to spread their good reputation will not associate with women who sell their beauty and talents for money.
Someone with an unsteady mind will seek the embrace of a woman who is only pretending to love them, because that woman is also thinking of someone else.
Someone without the ability to discern is lured by the embraces of deceitful women, which are as ruinous as the touch of a celestial enchantress who kills with desire.
The soft, jewelled arms of prostitutes are a hell into which degraded people fall.
Treacherous women, alcohol, and gambling are the companions of people who have been abandoned by the goddess of wealth.
Someone who is addicted to alcohol will not be feared by their enemies and will lose their fame.
Do not drink liquor, but if you must, drink only if you do not care about the esteem of wise people.

A drunkard's joy is painful even to his mother's face, so how much worse must it be in the presence of the wise? Even a mother who forgives her son's mistakes cannot bear to see him intoxicated, so how will the truly wise tolerate it?
Good shame turns its back on those who commit the great crime of drinking intoxicating liquor.
Giving money to buy unconsciousness is a sign of ignorance. It is foolish to spend wealth to lose awareness of oneself.
People who sleep are just like the dead, and people who drink toddy are just like people who drink poison because they lose their senses.
Someone who secretly drinks alcohol and loses their senses will have their condition discovered by their fellow townspeople, who will laugh at them every day.
Someone who drinks alcohol should stop claiming they never drink, because any wrongdoing they have hidden in their mind will be revealed the moment they lose their self-control.

Reasoning with a drunkard is like searching for someone who has drowned underwater with a torch. Just as a torch cannot help find a submerged person, logical arguments cannot reach the mind of someone who is heavily intoxicated.
When a sober person sees a drunkard, they should remember the exhaustion they themselves felt when they were drunk, which would help them stop drinking.
Even if you can win at gambling, you should not desire it, because what you win is like a fish swallowing the iron of a fishhook.
Is there any way for gamblers who lose a hundred to gain one to live a prosperous and good life? No, there is not.
If a ruler constantly talks about and plays with dice, his wealth and the income from it will go to his enemies.

There is nothing else that causes poverty like gambling, which creates many miseries and destroys a person's reputation. Gambling brings many sorrows, ruins one's fame, and leads them into extreme poverty.
Those who refuse to give up gambling, the gambling hall, and the skill of throwing dice will eventually lose all their wealth.
Those who are trapped by the goddess of gambling will never be satisfied and will suffer from hunger and pain. They will also experience misery in the afterlife.
If someone wastes their time in a gambling den, it will destroy their inherited wealth and good character.
Gambling destroys wealth, leads to falsehood, and removes grace, causing misery.
If a person gambles, they will lose clothing, wealth, food, fame, and learning. These five things will abandon the person who gambles and set their heart on it.
As a gambler loves the game more the more he loses, the soul loves the body more the more it suffers.
If food and work are either excessive or deficient, the three things medical writers count—wind, bile, and phlegm—will cause disease.
If you eat only after your previous meal has fully digested, you will not need any medicine for your body.
Eat only after your previous meal has digested, and consume food in the right measure to prolong the life of your body.
Know that your previous meal has been digested, and when you are very hungry, eat foods that do not change or disagree with your body.
If you eat a simple, consistent meal in moderation, you will not suffer from illness.
Someone who eats moderately experiences lasting pleasure, while a glutton who eats too much suffers from constant illness.
If someone eats without measuring their hunger and without considering the size of their stomach, they will suffer from countless diseases.
A doctor should first identify the disease, then find its cause, and finally determine the cure, and then treat it without making a mistake. This applies to both physical and social illnesses.
A skilled doctor should consider the patient's condition, the nature of the disease, and the season before treating them.
Medical treatment involves four things: the patient, the doctor, the medicine, and the person who administers it. Each of these four has its own four sub-categories.
Consistency in thought, word, and deed, and a sense of shame, are natural only to those born into a noble family.
People of noble birth do not lack good conduct, truth, and modesty. They naturally follow these three qualities without deviation.
A cheerful face, giving what you have, speaking kindly, and not insulting others are the four qualities of a truly noble person.
Even if they receive billions of wealth, people born into a noble family will not commit actions that degrade their family's honor.
Even if a person from an ancient family becomes poor, they will not lose their habit of giving.
Someone who lives to preserve their family's spotless honor will not stoop to deceitful acts, even in poverty.
The faults of a person from a noble family are seen as clearly as the dark spots on the moon.
If someone from a good family shows a lack of affection, people will doubt their ancestry.
The nature of the soil is shown by the plants that grow from it, and the nature of a person's family is shown by the words they speak.
If someone wants to gain a good reputation, they must have modesty, and if they want their family to be respected, they must be humble to everyone.
Even if an action is essential for your life, you should not do anything that would bring shame to your family.
Someone who wants to maintain their honour will not do anything dishonourable, even if it brings them fame.
In times of great prosperity, one should be humble, and in times of great adversity, one should maintain one's dignity.

People who fall from their high status are like hair that has fallen from a head. When people of noble birth lose their high position and dignity, they are considered as worthless as hair that has dropped from the head.
Even people who are as great as a mountain will be brought down if they do even a tiny, shameful act.
Bowing down to people who insult you and losing your self-respect brings no fame in this world and does not lead you to heaven, so what is the use of doing it?
It is better to be said to have died than to live by following those who disrespect you.
When a person of high birth loses their honour, a life that only preserves the body is not a cure for death.
Like a yak that dies if it loses its hair, a person of honour will give up their life if their honour is lost.
The world will forever praise and honor the memory of honorable people who choose to die rather than live with a ruined reputation.
A person's light is their courage to do great things, and their darkness is the thought of living without that courage.
All beings are the same in birth, but their work determines their different levels of worth.
Someone who is in a high position but lacks noble qualities is not truly high, and someone who is in a low position but lacks base qualities is not truly low.
Greatness belongs only to someone who guards themselves from straying, just like a faithful woman guards her chastity.

People with true greatness do difficult deeds in the proper way, even when they face hardships. True greatness is the absence of arrogance or pride, and it is shown by doing rare and difficult actions in the right manner.
Small-minded people do not have the desire to seek out, befriend, and learn from great people. They do not think about honoring the great and adopting their ways to elevate themselves.
When people who lack good character gain high status, wealth, or education, they naturally act with extreme arrogance.
Great people always remain humble, while petty people constantly admire and praise themselves.
True greatness is living without arrogance even when there is a reason to be proud, while meanness is swelling with vanity and stopping at the very edge of arrogance.
Great people hide the faults of others, while small people only point out their faults.
People say that all good qualities are simply a natural duty to those who recognize their responsibilities and live a virtuous life.

The good of great people is their good character, and no other good is found in any other good. The beauty of wise people is their good character, and all other external beauties are not included in any beauty. Good character is the only beauty of great people, and no other beauty is a beauty.
Love, modesty, benevolence, grace, and truth are the five pillars that support perfect goodness.
True penance is not killing, and true virtue is not speaking ill of others.
The strength of a capable person is their humility, which is the tool great people use to change their enemies.
The test of a person's worth is their ability to accept defeat even from someone they consider inferior.
What good is being good if you don't do good things for those who have hurt you?
Poverty is not a disgrace to someone who possesses the strength of good character and virtue.
People of perfect virtue are like the shore of the sea, and they never change even if ages pass.
If the great people lose their perfect virtue, the world can no longer bear its own weight.
If you are easy to approach and talk to, it is easy to learn good character and courtesy.
Having affection for others and being born into a harmonious family are the two qualities that make up good character.
People are not truly alike just because their bodies look similar. True likeness comes from having the same good qualities.
The world praises the character of those who live justly and usefully, benefiting others and themselves.
Even in jest, mocking someone is harmful, so wise people who understand human nature maintain good qualities even when they are dealing with enemies.
The world exists because it is supported by people of good character; without them, it would crumble to dust.
Even if someone has a sharp intellect like a file, they are just like a tree if they lack good human qualities.
It is shameful for wise people to lack good qualities and behave badly even towards those who show them no friendship and only do hateful things.
To someone who lacks good character and cannot mingle with others and rejoice, even the vast world in broad daylight feels like it is in darkness.
Wealth gained by someone without good character is useless, like pure milk that spoils when kept in a dirty container.
Someone who hoards great wealth but never enjoys it is as good as dead, because they have achieved nothing with their riches.
Someone who hoards wealth without giving to others, believing it can solve everything, will be born into a miserable life.
People who only want to gather wealth and do not desire fame are a burden to the earth.
What will a wealthy person who is disliked by everyone expect to survive after they die?
People who do not share their wealth with others and do not enjoy it themselves are truly destitute, even if they possess crores of riches.
Great wealth is a disease to someone who does not use it for themselves or give it to worthy people.
The wealth of someone who does not help the poor is like a beautiful woman who grows old alone.
The wealth of someone who is disliked by everyone is like a poisonous tree bearing fruit in the middle of a town.
Others will take and enjoy the wealth that someone gathers without showing love, without practicing charity, and while only causing themselves suffering.

When rich and generous people experience a brief period of poverty, it is like rain clouds temporarily becoming thin or empty. Even though this short-lived poverty causes them to temporarily stop giving to others, they will eventually become wealthy again and continue to help the world, just as the clouds will eventually rain again.
True shame is shrinking from doing evil, while other shame is simply the natural bashfulness of beautiful women.
Food, clothing, and other basic needs are common to all living beings, but modesty is a special quality of good people.

All living beings reside in a physical body, and similarly, the virtue of modesty is the home of perfection. Just as a spirit cannot function without a body, perfection cannot exist without the feeling of modesty.
Shame is a beautiful ornament for people of dignity, and without it, their proud walk looks like a sickness.
The world considers a person to be the home of shame if they feel ashamed for their own wrongdoing and for the wrongdoing of others.
Great people do not desire the wide world without making modesty their protective fence.
Someone who values modesty would rather give up their life than give up their modesty. They would not abandon their modesty to save their life.
Virtue will abandon someone who shamelessly commits acts that other people are ashamed of.
A lack of good manners ruins one's family lineage, and a complete lack of shame ruins all of a person's goodness and well-being.
The actions of people who have no shame in their hearts are like a wooden puppet moved by a string that is made to look alive. These people are not truly alive, just like the wooden puppet.

Even though the world wanders around doing many different jobs, it ultimately depends on the plowman to survive. Therefore, even though farming is hard and full of suffering, it is the most important and primary occupation.
Farmers are the linchpin of the world because they support everyone else who cannot farm.
Those who live by ploughing and eating their own food are the ones who truly live. Everyone else lives by bowing to others and eating what they are given.
Farmers who have abundant grain will see the umbrellas of many kings come under their own king's umbrella.
Someone who works with their own hands to earn their food will not beg from others, but will give to those who ask.
Even ascetics who claim to have given up all worldly desires depend on farmers to survive, so if the farmers stop working, even the ascetics will starve.
If you plow the soil until it is reduced to a quarter of its original weight, you can grow abundant crops without using any manure.
Applying manure is better than ploughing, and weeding is better than watering. However, protecting the crop from harm is even better than all of these.
If the owner does not personally attend to his land, it will become like an angry wife and yield no crops.

The good earth will laugh to see people sitting idle and complaining that they are poor. The earth provides wealth to those who work, so she mocks those who do nothing and still complain about being poor.
Nothing is more painful than poverty, and poverty itself is the most painful thing.
Poverty is a terrible sin that deprives a person of both present and future happiness.
The craving that people call poverty destroys a person's ancient lineage and their dignified speech.
Poverty causes even people from good families to become tired and utter mean words.
Wanton poverty is a great misery that brings many other miseries with it.
Even if a poor person speaks with deep understanding and conveys good, profound thoughts, people will not listen to or value their words, and their speech will ultimately go to waste.
A person who is poor and lacks virtue will be treated like a stranger even by his own mother.
Will the poverty that almost killed me yesterday come to bother me again today?
Someone can sleep in the middle of a fire, but in poverty, not even a moment of sleep is possible.
The destitute who do not renounce their lives cause their neighbor's salt and gruel to go to waste.
If you find someone who can give, you should ask them for help. If they refuse, the blame is theirs, not yours.
Even begging for something brings joy if the requested items are given without causing any distress.
It is beautiful to beg from someone who has a generous heart and understands their duty to give.
Asking for something from someone who never even thinks of refusing in their dreams is just like giving to others.

Poor people stand before someone and beg because there are people in the world who give without hiding their wealth or saying no. They do this because they know they will be helped, rather than dying from shame.
If you see someone who does not hide their wealth and is free from the disease of begging, the poverty and suffering of the beggar will completely disappear.
When someone gives without insulting or scorning the receiver, the receiver's heart is filled with joy.
If there were no beggars, the movement of the cool wide world would be like wooden puppets being moved by a string.
What glory is there for those who give if there are no people who ask for and receive their help? Without people who ask, there is no one to praise the givers, so the givers do not get any glory.
Someone who asks for help should not get angry at a refusal, because their own suffering from poverty is proof enough of their need.
It is billions of times better to not beg, even from excellent people who happily give whatever they have without hiding it.
If the Creator of the world has made begging a way of life, then he too should wander and perish.
There is nothing harder than the stubbornness of someone who gives up trying to work and instead believes they can end the misery of poverty by begging.
The dignity of someone who does not beg even when they have no way to live is a greatness that the whole world cannot contain.
Even if the food is just thin gruel made with water, nothing is sweeter than eating what you earned through your own hard work.
There is nothing more shameful for a person's tongue than begging for water even for a thirsty cow.
I ask all beggars to never beg from people who hide their wealth. It is better to not ask for anything at all than to receive a reluctant gift.
The unsafe raft of begging will split when it strikes the rock of refusal.
Thinking of the suffering of beggars melts the heart, but thinking of the cruelty of refusing them breaks it completely.
When someone who asks is told "no," they lose their life, so where can the life of the person who denies them hide?

Bad people look exactly like good people in outward form, but we have never seen any other species that resembles humans so closely. Because they look so much like humans, their bad character is not easily noticed.

People who lack a sense of right and wrong are considered wealthier because they do not worry about doing good deeds or the consequences of their actions, while those who understand what is good are constantly troubled by anxiety and fear.
The base act like the gods because they do whatever they want without any restrictions. They can do whatever they wish because no one controls them.
When a base person sees someone who acts even lower than they do, they feel superior and become arrogant.
The conduct of base people is driven by fear, and if that fails, the hope of gaining what they desire provides a little bit of discipline.
Base people are like a beaten drum because they spread the secrets they have heard.
Someone who is stingy will not shake off the food stuck to their hands for anyone except those who would break their jaws with their clenched fists.
Good people give to you as soon as you tell them your problems, but bad people only give when you pressure and torture them like crushing sugarcane.
When a lowly person sees others wearing nice clothes and eating good food, they become jealous and will deliberately look for faults to accuse them of.
When a calamity strikes, a base person will quickly sell themselves. They are fit for nothing else.
Is the woman wearing heavy earrings a goddess, a beautiful peacock, or a human woman? My mind is completely bewildered trying to figure out who she is.

When the beautiful woman returned my gaze, her counter glance felt like a weaponized arrow bringing an army to attack me. Her looking back at me felt like a striking force bringing troops to fight me.
I never knew what was called death before, but I understand it now; it is the large, fighting eyes that carry the qualities of a woman.
The woman's simple and feminine appearance is contradicted by her eyes, which seem to drink the life of anyone who looks at them.
Is the young woman's gaze a deadly weapon, a darting eye, or a frightened deer? It possesses all three qualities.
If her cruel, arched eyebrows were to hide her eyes, they would not cause me the sorrow that makes me tremble.
A piece of cloth draped over a woman's firm breasts is like a cloth placed over the eyes of a rutting elephant.
My power that once terrified my enemies in battle has been destroyed by the sight of my beloved's beautiful brow.
What use are other jewels to a woman who is already adorned with the meek looks of a fawn and modesty?
Unlike wine which only gives pleasure when drunk, love gives pleasure just by being seen.
Her painted eyes have two kinds of glances, one that causes pain and the other that cures that pain.
A stolen, furtive glance from her eyes is greater than half the pleasure of sexual embrace.
She looked at him and, out of shyness, bowed her head, which was like watering the growing crop of love between them.
When I look at her, she looks down at the ground, but when I look away, she looks at me and smiles gently.
She does not look directly at me, but instead looks with one eye half-closed as if smiling to herself.
Even if someone speaks harsh words like a stranger, you will quickly understand that they are actually friendly and hold no hatred in their heart.

Even if someone speaks harsh words without any anger and looks at you like an enemy, they are actually showing signs of their love. They are just pretending to be strangers on the outside while caring deeply on the inside.
When I look at her, the tender maid smiles gently, and that soft smile brings a comforting beauty to her swaying form.

Lovers have the natural habit of looking at each other in public as if they were complete strangers. They act as though they do not know each other, even though they secretly feel a deep, joyful love.
When two people in love look into each other's eyes, words are useless.
All the pleasures of the five senses—sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch—can be fully experienced at the same time with a woman wearing shining bangles.
The cure for a disease is something different from it, but for the disease caused by this woman, she herself is the cure.
Is the lotus-eyed lord's heaven as sweet as sleeping in the soft arms of a beloved?
The woman has a fire in her that burns when I move away and cools when I get close. Where did she get this unique fire to put it in my heart?
The shoulders of the woman with flower-adorned hair bring me joy just like the exact things I desired when I first wished for them.
The simple maiden's shoulders are made of ambrosia, and when I embrace her, my withered life puts forth its buds again.
Embracing a beautiful, dark-complexioned woman is as pleasant as staying at home and enjoying the food you earned and shared with others.
A tight embrace where not even a breath of air can pass between two loving partners is sweet.
Married people gain the benefits of love through the joys of a lover's tryst: a lover's quarrel, reconciling after realizing the mistake, and reuniting.
As people learn more and discover their past ignorance, repeated intimacy with a beautifully adorned woman only creates an endless desire for more.
O anicham flower, may you flourish, for you have a very delicate nature, but my beloved is even more delicate than you.
My heart, you become confused when you see flowers, thinking they resemble her eyes, which many people get to see.
She has a body like a tender shoot, teeth like pearls, breath like a fragrant scent, and eyes like a sharp spear, all with shoulders like bamboo.
If the lilies could see the woman with the beautiful jeweled eyes, they would bow their heads and look at the ground in shame because they could never match her eyes.
If a woman wears anicham flowers without removing their stems, her delicate waist will be pained and no auspicious drums will be beaten for her.
The stars are confused and moving wildly because they cannot tell the difference between the moon and the woman's face.
Does this woman's face have any blemishes, just like the phases of the waxing and waning moon?
If you could shine like a woman's face, you would be worthy of my love.
Moon, if you want to look like the face of the woman with flower-like eyes, then do not appear where many people can see you.
The soft anicham flower and the swan's down are painful to the delicate feet of women, just like the thorny nerunji fruit.
The water oozing from the white teeth of the soft-spoken woman is as sweet as milk mixed with honey.
The love between me and this woman is exactly like the bond between the soul and the body. The soul and the body cannot be separated from each other, and we are just as inseparable.
O image in my pupil, leave because there is no room for my beautiful-browed beloved.
When the woman adorned with fine ornaments is with me, she is like life to my soul; when she leaves me, she is like death to my soul.
If I could forget the qualities of the woman with bright, battling eyes, I would remember you; but I never forget her, so I do not remember you.
My lover's subtle form never leaves my eyes, and he does not mind even if I blink.
Because my lover lives inside my eyes, I do not paint them with kohl, knowing that he would have to hide if I did.
My lover lives in my heart, so I am afraid to eat hot food because I don't want it to burn him.
The speaker keeps their eyes open so their lover hiding inside them does not disappear, because the townspeople will call him unloving.
My lover is always happy inside my heart, but the people of the town, not knowing this, say he is unloving and lives far away.
For those who suffer from unfulfilled passion, there is no help as effective as the palmyra horse.
My body and soul, unable to bear the pain of separation, have decided to abandon shame and ride the palmyra horse.
I once possessed modesty and true manliness, but today I only have the palmyra horse ridden by lustful people.
The strong current of lust sweeps away the raft of shame and good manliness.
The girl with the small, garland-like bracelets gave me the palmyra horse and the sorrow I feel at night.
My eyes won't sleep because of my beloved, so I will think of climbing the palmyra tree even at midnight.
There is no birth as noble as a woman who, though suffering from a sea-like lust, does not ride the palmyra horse.
Lust betrays its secrecy and becomes public, without considering that the woman is highly soft, chaste, and worthy of pity.
My love, thinking no one knows it, wanders confusedly in the streets.
Fools laugh at me to my face because they have never experienced the pain I have suffered.
My life is sustained because the rumor of our love is spreading, and to my good luck, most people do not know the real reason behind it.
The town, not knowing the value of the woman with flower-like eyes, spread a rumor about me, which helped me.
Hearing the town talk about my love is a gain for me, as if I have already obtained what I have not yet gotten.
The rumor circulating in town fuels my passion, and without it, my love would lose its vitality and fade away.
As drinking liquor becomes more delightful the more one drinks, lust becomes more delightful the more it is talked about.
I saw my lover for only a single day, but the resulting rumors spread throughout the world like a snake swallowing the moon.

The town's gossip acts as manure, and my mother's harsh words act as water, making this love-sickness grow. The town's gossip provides the fertilizer, and my mother's scolding provides the water for this love-sickness to grow.
Trying to stop passion with gossip is like trying to put out a fire with ghee.
When the one who told me not to fear has left me, causing others to feel shame, why should I be ashamed of the rumors they are spreading?
The town is spreading the rumor I want, so my lover will now grant my wish.
If you are not leaving, tell me. If you are returning quickly, tell those who will be alive then.
His very presence was once a source of joy, but now even being close to him is painful because of the fear of separation.
It is hard to trust someone who understands you, because even a knowledgeable lover may eventually leave.
If the one who said "fear not" and gave his love should depart, is there any fault for those who trusted his clear words?
If you want to save my life, you must prevent my destined husband from leaving, because if he departs, it will be difficult for us to meet again.
If someone is cruel enough to say they are leaving, it is pointless to hope they will return and show love.
The bangles slipping from my hand are announcing that my lord is leaving.
Living in a town where there are no friends is painful, but parting from a beloved lover is even more painful.
Fire burns when touched, but love's sickness burns even when people are apart.
Many people can endure the pain of separation and continue to live, but I cannot.
I want to hide my love sickness from others, but it only swells like a spring to those who draw water from it. The more I try to conceal my suffering, the more it grows.
I cannot hide this love sickness, nor can I bring myself to tell the person who caused it.
My soul acts as a pole, and on either end of it, lust and shame hang like burdens on my body, which cannot bear their weight.
There is a sea of lust, but there is no raft to cross it safely. This is a sea of the pain of love, and there is no safe boat to swim across it.
Someone who causes sorrow even in friendship, what can they not do when they become enemies?
The pleasure of love is like the sea, but the pain of love is even greater.
I swim the fierce waves of love but cannot see its shore, and I am alone even in the middle of the night.
The night lulls all living creatures to sleep, leaving me alone without any companion.
The long, slow nights of these days are even crueler than the cruelty of the cruel person who is torturing me.
If my eyes could travel to my lover just like my mind, they would not have to swim in this flood of tears.
The incurable disease of love happened because my eyes showed me the lover, so why are those same eyes crying and asking me to show him to them today?
The eyes that looked without understanding the consequences back then are now suffering in sorrow without realizing that they brought this upon themselves.
The eyes eagerly looked at her lover on that day, but today they weep on their own, which is a laughable sight.
These painted eyes have given me an incurable, inescapable love disease and then stopped weeping, drying up from their own tears.
My eyes caused a lust greater than the sea, and now they suffer sleeplessly from that same pain.
The eyes that caused my love-sickness have themselves fallen into the same suffering, and I find this very sweet. It feels like a relief to see them weep sleeplessly, suffering just as I do.
The eyes that once gazed with such tender longing at the lover they desired should suffer through sleepless nights of sorrow today, until all their tears completely dry up.
There is someone here who loved me with his words but not with his heart, and my eyes cannot find peace without seeing him.
The eyes of someone in love do not sleep when their lover is away, and they do not sleep when the lover is present. In both situations, the eyes endure unbearable agony.
It is not hard for the people of this town to know a secret when someone has eyes like mine that reveal what is hidden in the heart.
I consented to my lover's absence, so now that I have turned pale from the pain of missing him, who can I tell about my fading complexion?
The paleness on my body creeps and spreads, proudly claiming that the lover created it.
He took my beauty and modesty and left me with disease and a pale complexion.
I think of his words and speak of his excellence, yet this pallor has come, which is deceitful.
My lover left, and my body grew pale.

Just as darkness waits for a lamp to fade, a woman's pallor waits for her lover's embrace to weaken. This fading happens when his tight embrace slightly loosens, and it might also happen if they are separated.
While I was lying in my lover's embrace, I unknowingly shifted a little to the side, and at that very moment, a paleness spread over me as if it were being scooped up.
People blame her for becoming pale, but no one says that he is the one who left her.
If the person who convinced me to accept this separation is truly well, then my body should turn pale.
It is good to be called pale if people do not insult the lover who made me agree to our separation by withholding his affection.
Someone who is loved by the person they love has obtained the stoneless fruit of love.
The love that a beloved shows to someone who loves them is like the rain that falls on living beings.
The pride of living belongs only to those who are loved in return by the one they love.

Even if someone is highly respected by society, they are considered unlucky and lacking in goodness if they are not loved by the person they love. If a woman is not loved by the husband she desires, she is considered unfortunate.
What good can someone who does not love us in return do for us?
It is painful if love is felt by only one person, but it is pleasant when both sides feel it equally, just like a balanced load on a carrying pole.
The god of love, who only acts on one side, does not see the pain and sorrow caused by the change in my complexion.
There is no one in the world as hard-hearted as someone who lives without receiving a single kind word from the person they love.
Even though the man I love does not return my affection, any word spoken about him is sweet to my ears.
My heart, live on! You are telling your deep sorrow to people who do not love you. Instead, try to empty the sea that is causing you this sorrow, because that is an easier task.

Love is sweeter than wine because thinking about past intimacy creates an endless, rapturous delight. Even when separated, simply remembering the joy of being together brings a happiness that outlasts the temporary pleasure of drinking liquor.
Thinking of one's beloved removes the pain of separation, so love is always sweet.
I feel like I'm about to sneeze but it doesn't happen, and I feel like my lover is about to think of me but he doesn't.
He is always in my heart, so am I always in his heart?
Someone who keeps me out of his heart is not ashamed to keep entering my heart.
I am still alive only because I remember the happy days I spent with him. If I did not have those memories, how could I possibly stay alive?
Even when I try to forget my lover, the pain of separation burns my heart; what will happen to me if I actually manage to forget?
Even if I think of him constantly, my beloved will not get angry, and isn't this the great favor he does for me?
My life is fading away because I keep thinking about the cruelty of the person who used to say we were one and the same.
O Moon, live on and do not set so that I can see with my eyes the one who left me but never left my mind.
How shall I host a feast for the dream that brought my beloved's messenger?
If my fish-like eyes close in sleep as I beg, I will tell my lover in a dream about the life I have survived.
My life continues because I see in my dreams the one who does not show me kindness when I am awake.
In dreams, I find pleasure because the dream brings me the lover who does not visit me when I am awake.
Seeing the beloved in waking life was pleasant at that time, and seeing him in a dream is also pleasant right now.
If wakefulness did not exist to break the dream, the lover who visits me in my dreams would never leave.
The cruel person who does not show kindness when awake torments me in my dreams. Why does this person who is unkind in person cause me pain in my dreams?
When I am asleep, my lover rests on my shoulders, and when I wake up, he quickly enters my heart.
Women who do not see their lovers in dreams will blame their lovers for not visiting them in waking life.
The women of the town say my lover has left me in my waking life, but they do not see him in my dreams.
Oh evening! You are not the evening of the past, but the time that devours the lives of women who have been with their lovers.
O dim evening, hail! You have lost your light just like me. Is your mate also cruel-eyed like my spouse?
The evening that once used to come trembling and pale now brings me an aversion to life and increasing sorrow.
When my lover is away, the evening comes like a merciless killer arriving at a slaughter.

What good have I done to the morning, and what evil to the evening? The speaker laments that the morning used to bring relief from the pain of separation, but now it brings sorrow, and the evening used to bring joy in the beloved's presence, but now it brings grief.
I did not know that the evening could cause such suffering when my husband was with me and never left me alone. I only learned about the pain of the evening after he departed.
This disease of love buds in the morning, grows all day, and blooms in the evening.
The shepherd's flute now acts as a messenger for the fiery evening that burns like a flame, and it sounds like a weapon that kills.
When evening comes and confuses the mind, the whole town will be plunged into sorrow just as I am.
My life, which had not died from the pain of separation, now dies in this bewitching evening as I think of my lover who has gone to seek wealth.
Because she is crying for her lover who left, her eyes have lost their brightness and are now ashamed to look at the fragrant flowers.
Tears rolling from discolored eyes seem to reveal to others that the person we love is not showing us any affection.
The shoulders that swelled with joy on the day of the wedding now look thin and announce the lover's departure.
Because the lover left, the shoulders lost their former beauty and fullness and became thin, causing the green gold bracelets to slip off.
The speaker's wasted arms, once beautiful but now bare of bracelets, are telling everyone about the cruelty of a pitiless person.
I am deeply hurt to hear people call my lover cruel just because my shoulders have grown thin and my armlets have slipped off.
Will you gain any glory by going to tell my cruel lover about the pain of my withering shoulders and the noise they make?
When I loosened my embracing arms, the forehead of the woman with the golden armlet turned pale.
When a cool breeze entered our embrace, the woman's large, cool eyes lost their color.
The lover's eyes became pale and sad when she saw that her own forehead had turned pale from the cold breeze, realizing that her beauty was fading just like the complexion of her body.
My heart, can you not think of some medicine that can cure this incurable disease?
My heart, live on! Since he does not love you, your longing for him is just foolishness.
O heart, why do you sit here and suffer thinking of him when he has no pity for you? Since he caused this sorrowful disease, he will not come to your rescue.
O heart, take these eyes with you when you go to him, because they are so eager to see him that they will otherwise eat me up.
Even though he does not love me back, can I really abandon him and think he hates me?
When you see your lover who removes your sulking by making love, you do not sulk, yet you now falsely burn with anger thinking they are cruel.
O good heart, you must give up either lust or shame, because I cannot endure both of them at the same time.
You are a fool, my heart, for chasing after the one who has left you, while you mourn that he does not show pity or love.
My heart, since your lover lives inside you, why do you go looking for him outside?
If I keep the person who left me in my heart, I will lose the inner beauty I still have.
Lust acts like an axe that breaks down the door of a woman's modesty, which is locked with the bolt of shame.
Lust is a merciless power that rules my mind even in the middle of the night.
I try to hide my lust, but it bursts out like a sneeze without any warning.
I used to think I was full of self-control, but my hidden desire has broken through my concealment and been exposed in public.
The dignity that does not pursue someone who has left you is something that someone who is in love cannot understand.
What kind of sorrow is this love sickness that makes me want to follow my lover who has left me, and how is it excellent?
When the person I love does what I desire out of love, I forget all shame.
The sweet, humble words of a deceitful lover who is an expert in many tricks are the weapon that breaks a woman's resolve.
I went away pretending to be angry, but when I saw my heart starting to unite with him, I embraced him.
Can people whose hearts melt like fat in the fire really say they will stand aloof and feign a quarrel after being together?
My eyes have lost their brightness from watching for his return, and my fingers have worn down from counting the days he has been gone.
If I forget my lover today, my shoulders will lose their beauty and my bracelets will slip off.

A lover who went abroad seeking victory with his enthusiasm as his only companion, left me because he did not want to enjoy happiness with me or have me as a companion. I am still alive only because I long to see him return and reject those other pursuits.
My heart is filled with rapture and climbs up the branches of a tree to look for my lover who left me, as I think of him returning with his love.
I just want to gaze at my husband until I am completely satisfied, and then the pallor on my slender shoulders will naturally fade away.
My lover should come to me one day, and when he does, I will fully enjoy him so that all my agonizing sorrow is destroyed.
When my beloved returns, should I sulk at him for delaying his arrival, or should I cry from my own helplessness, or should I do both?
May the king fight and win, and let me be united with my wife to feast this evening.
For those who wait and yearn for the return of a distant spouse, one day feels as long as seven.
If a woman's heart breaks from the pain of separation and she dies, what is the use of her meeting or embracing me afterward?
Even if you hide your feelings, your painted eyes refuse to stay silent and will tell me that you do not want to be separated from me.
The simple woman with beautiful eyes and bamboo-like shoulders has an abundance of feminine modesty.
There is a hidden meaning in a woman's beauty, like the thread that is visible inside a string of jewels.
A young woman's budding smile hides a secret, much like a fragrance concealed inside an unbloomed bud.

The secret signal my wife sent me when she left, hiding it from everyone else, holds the cure for my deep sorrow. Her playful glance, while wearing her tight bangles, also contains the medicine to heal my pain.
His loving embrace comforts me, but it also makes me realize he will soon leave me and no longer love me.
My armlets knew about my lover's mental separation from me before I did. They fell off because they sensed his heart was no longer with me, even though his body was still here.
My lover left me yesterday, and it has been seven days since my body turned sallow.
She looked at her armlets, her tender shoulders, and her feet, and this was her way of telling him to come with her.
Expressing love-sickness through the eyes and praying for relief is an even more feminine trait than a woman's natural womanhood.
The joy felt when thinking of someone and the happiness seen when looking at them belong to love, not to wine.
When a woman's desire grows as large as a palmyra fruit, she should not sulk with her lover even as much as a millet grain.
Even if he slighted me and did only what he wanted, my eyes would not be at peace without seeing him.
My friend, I went to see him ready to pretend to be angry, but my heart forgot my plan and was eager to embrace him.

When I am close to my husband, I cannot see his faults, just like eyes that fail to see the kohl stick that paints them. Even though I had been thinking about his past mistakes when we were apart, seeing him in person makes me forget them entirely.
When I see my husband, I do not see any of his faults, and when I do not see him, I do not see anything except his faults.
Why should a wife feign anger and quarrel with her husband, knowing that her anger will not last long, just as someone jumps into a stream knowing it will sweep them away?
Your breast is like wine to drunkards, who keep wanting it even when it brings them disgrace.
Love is more delicate than a flower, and only a few people truly understand its nature and experience its full pleasure.
She initially showed her anger with her eyes, but she forgot the quarrel and embraced him more eagerly than he did.
Even though you see that his heart belongs entirely to him and stays by his side, why do you not stand by me and instead melt only for him?
O my heart, even though you know he does not love me, you still go to him thinking he will not get angry.
Why do you follow him at your own will, leaving me, because you think the ruined have no friends?
My heart, you will not sulk first and then enjoy him; who will then consult you about such things?
The heart fears being without a lover, and it also fears losing the lover once they are gained, which causes endless sorrow.
My heart feels like it is eating me when I think of my lover's cruelty while I am alone.
I have forgotten my shame because my worthless, foolish mind cannot forget him.
My heart, which loves him deeply, thinks only of his greatness and refuses to despise him, because it fears that doing so would bring disgrace upon itself.
If someone's own heart does not help them when they are in pain, who else will support them?
It is easy for strangers to be unfriendly when one's own heart is not one's own.
Feign sulk and do not embrace him so that we can watch his distress for a little while.
A little bit of sulking adds spice to love, but keeping it up too long makes it bitter, just like too much salt ruins a dish.
Leaving someone who is sulking without an embrace is like adding to the pain of someone who is already suffering.
Not comforting a partner who is upset and pouting is like cutting a dried-up vine right at the root.
Even good and virtuous men find the pouting of wives with flower-like eyes to be a lovely grace.
Love without any conflict, whether big or small, is like a fruit that is either too ripe or too unripe.
A lover's quarrel causes pain because they worry the happy reunion will be delayed.
What good is grieving when there is no lover to understand the cause of the sorrow?
Water is pleasant in the shade, and sulking is pleasant only with loved ones. Just as water is refreshing near the shade, arguments are enjoyable only with people you love.
The heart desires to reunite with the person who left it pining and ignored its sulking. This intense desire is the sole reason for this longing.
You are a prostitute. All women look at you with desire, so I will not embrace your chest.
A man sneezed while his lover was sulking, hoping she would finally speak to him and wish him a long life.
Even if I wear a garland of branch-flowers, she will angrily accuse me of wearing it to show off to another woman.
When I said I loved her more than anyone else, she sulked and asked, "More than whom, more than whom?
I told my lover I would never leave her in this life, and she cried, thinking we would have to part in the next one.
I told my lover that I had been thinking of her, and she started crying and pretending to be upset because she thought I had forgotten her.
When I sneezed, she first blessed me but then immediately became angry and cried, asking who I was thinking of when I sneezed.
When I suppressed a sneeze, she cried that I was hiding from her the thoughts of my own people.
Even when I try to soothe her and apologize for my mistakes, she gets angry and accuses me of behaving the exact same way with other women.
Even when I silently think about and gaze at her incomparable beauty, she gets angry and asks, "Who are you thinking of and comparing me to?
Although he has no faults, pretending to be upset makes him love me more.
The small pain caused by a lover's quarrel makes the great love they show afterward even more valuable, even if it seems to have faded a little.
Is there a heaven more blissful than the feigned dislike between lovers whose hearts are as united as earth and water?

In a lingering embrace where a lover refuses to let go, there is a weapon that breaks my heart. This weapon represents the feigned anger and sweet words of affection used to keep the couple together, which ultimately destroy my resolve.
Even if someone is without fault, there is a special pleasure in being estranged from the delicate shoulders of the woman he loves.
It is sweeter to digest a meal than to eat it, and it is sweeter to quarrel in love than to be united.
The one who yields in a lovers' quarrel is the true winner, and this is proven when they reunite.
Will we get to enjoy the sweetness of making love again, which causes her forehead to sweat, if we have another playful quarrel?
May the woman with shining jewels continue to sulk, and may the night be prolonged so I can keep pleading with her.
Feigned dislike adds spice to love, and the pleasure grows when they finally unite.
